title: Investigating the Conformational Dynamics of a Y-Family DNA Polymerase during Its Folding and Binding to DNA and a Nucleotide.
authors: Chu, Xiakun; Suo, Zucai; Wang, Jin
one_liner_zh: 该文用基于结构的模型研究Y家族DNA聚合酶DPO4与DNA及核苷酸结合过程中的构象动态，属于广义蛋白-DNA互作体系，方法为物理模拟，但对象非TF-DNA，故评6分。
abstract: During DNA polymerization, the Y-family DNA polymerases are capable of bypassing various DNA damage, which can stall the replication fork progression. It has been well acknowledged that the structures of the Y-family DNA polymerases have been naturally evolved to undertake this vital task. However, the mechanisms of how these proteins utilize their unique structural and conformational dynamical features to perform the translesion DNA synthesis are less understood. Here, we developed structure-based models to study the precatalytic DNA polymerization process, including DNA and nucleotide binding to DPO4, a paradigmatic Y-family polymerase from Sulfolobus solfataricus. We studied the interplay between the folding and the conformational dynamics of DPO4 and found that DPO4 undergoes first unraveling (unfolding) and then folding for accomplishing the functional "open-to-closed" conformational transition. DNA binding dynamically modulates the conformational equilibrium in DPO4 during the stepwise binding through different types of interactions, leading to different conformational distributions of DPO4 at different DNA binding stages. We observed that nucleotide binding induces modulation of a few contacts surrounding the active site of the DPO4-DNA complex associated with a high free energy barrier. Our simulation results resonate with the experimental evidence that the conformational change at the active site led by nucleotide is the rate-limiting step of nucleotide incorporation. In combination with localized frustration analyses, we underlined the importance of DPO4 conformational dynamics and fluctuations in facilitating DNA and nucleotide binding. Our findings offer mechanistic insights into the processes of DPO4 conformational dynamics associated with the substrate binding and contribute to the understanding of the "structure-dynamics-function" relationship in the Y-family DNA polymerases.
abstract_zh: 在DNA聚合过程中，Y家族DNA聚合酶能够绕过多种DNA损伤，这些损伤可能阻碍复制叉的推进。众所周知，Y家族DNA聚合酶的结构经过自然进化，以承担这一关键任务。然而，这些蛋白质如何利用其独特的结构和构象动态特征来执行跨损伤DNA合成的机制尚不十分清楚。在此，我们开发了基于结构的模型，以研究催化前的DNA聚合过程，包括DNA和核苷酸与DPO4（一种来自硫磺矿硫化叶菌（Sulfolobus solfataricus）的典型Y家族聚合酶）的结合。我们研究了DPO4折叠与构象动态之间的相互作用，发现DPO4经历先解折叠（unfolding）后折叠的过程，以实现功能性的“开放到闭合”构象转变。DNA结合通过不同类型的相互作用动态调节DPO4在逐步结合过程中的构象平衡，导致DPO4在不同DNA结合阶段呈现不同的构象分布。我们观察到核苷酸结合诱导了DPO4-DNA复合物活性位点周围少数接触的调节，并伴随高自由能屏障。我们的模拟结果与实验证据相呼应，即核苷酸引起的活性位点构象变化是核苷酸掺入的限速步骤。结合局部挫析分析，我们强调了DPO4构象动态和波动在促进DNA和核苷酸结合中的重要性。我们的发现为DPO4构象动态与底物结合相关过程提供了机制性见解，并有助于理解Y家族DNA聚合酶中的“结构-动态-功能”关系。
